original_question: Let K be a regular non-polar compact subset of R with leftmost endpoint α, and let μ_K be its equilibrium measure. Assume that μ_K([α,c]) is rational for every c∈R\K. Characterize such sets K. In particular, must every such K be a polynomial generalized Julia set, or equivalently must there exist a sequence (f_n) of admissible polynomials such that, with F_n=f_n∘f_{n-1}∘···∘f_1, the inverse-image sets F_n^{-1}([-1,1]) form a decreasing sequence and K=⋂_{n=1}^∞ F_n^{-1}([-1,1])?
correct_elements: Your draft correctly matches the hypothesis of Problem 9: K is a regular non-polar compact subset of ℝ, α is the leftmost endpoint of K, μ_K is the equilibrium measure, and μ_K([α,c]) is assumed rational for every c in ℝ outside K. It also captures the two specific directions asked in the paper: whether such a K must be a polynomial generalized Julia set, and whether one can realize K as a decreasing intersection of inverse images of [-1,1] under admissible polynomials.
missing_details: The paper asks the weaker question “What can we say about K?” rather than demanding a full characterization; “Characterize such sets K” is broader than the official formulation.
Here “regular” means regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem; that should be stated explicitly in a stand-alone version.
The term “polynomial generalized Julia set” is not self-contained unless one defines J(f_n) as the complement in ℂ of the Montel normality domain of the compositions F_n = f_n ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_1.

The exact definition of a regular polynomial sequence from Section 1.2 is missing: if f_n(z) = Σ_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j with d_n ≥ 2, then there must exist constants A_1, A_2, A_3 > 0 such that |a_{n,d_n}| ≥ A_1, |a_{n,j}| ≤ A_2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0 ≤ j < d_n, and log|a_{n,d_n}| ≤ A_3 d_n for all n.
The exact definition of an admissible polynomial is missing: a real polynomial T_N of degree N ≥ 2 with N real simple zeros and N−1 critical points y_i satisfying |T_N(y_i)| ≥ 1.

The draft says “or equivalently,” but Problem 9 does not state or prove that the admissible-polynomial realization is equivalent to being a polynomial generalized Julia set; it poses this as a further question.
The quantifier is specifically over c in ℝ outside K, not over complex c outside K.
In the second question, the monotonicity requirement that the sets F_n^{-1}([-1,1]) form a decreasing sequence should remain explicit.
refined_question: Let K ⊂ ℝ be a non-polar compact set that is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, let α = min K be its leftmost endpoint, and let μ_K denote its equilibrium measure. Assume that μ_K([α,c]) ∈ ℚ for every c ∈ ℝ outside K. What can be said about K? In particular, must K be a polynomial generalized Julia set, i.e. K = J(f_n) for some regular polynomial sequence (f_n), where F_n = f_n ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_1, each f_n(z) = Σ_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j has degree d_n ≥ 2, and there exist constants A_1, A_2, A_3 > 0 such that |a_{n,d_n}| ≥ A_1, |a_{n,j}| ≤ A_2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0 ≤ j < d_n, and log|a_{n,d_n}| ≤ A_3 d_n for all n? Moreover, does this hypothesis imply that there exists a sequence of admissible real polynomials (f_n) (meaning: if deg f_n = d_n, then f_n has d_n real simple zeros and d_n−1 critical points y with |f_n(y)| ≥ 1) such that the inverse-image sets F_n^{-1}([-1,1]) form a decreasing sequence and K = ⋂_{n=1}^∞ F_n^{-1}([-1,1])?
justification: The draft is aimed directly at Problem 9: it reproduces the same rationality hypothesis on μ_K([α,c]) and the same two follow-up questions. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one has to import the definitions from Section 1.2 of generalized Julia sets and regular polynomial sequences, and the definition of admissible polynomials from the discussion immediately preceding Theorem 3.1. The main corrections are that the official problem does not ask for a complete classification, and it does not present the admissible-polynomial realization as a proved equivalent reformulation.
